title: That Didn't Last Long
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate downgrades Costco just seven weeks after upgrading it. On 21 September he upgraded Costco to a BUY for the first time in years, at about $890-900, when the forward P/E had fallen to about 36, its lowest in years, and it barely qualified as a buy under his framework. Since then the stock has soared to over $1,060, up 23% year to date, without any phenomenal earnings to justify the move: investors simply realised Costco was cheap and rushed in. The forward P/E is now over 42 and his DCF fair value is about $833, so the stock trades about 21% above fair value. He stresses he is not saying it is ridiculously expensive, only that the rare cheap entry has passed: it is a great Hall of Fame business to hold if you already own it, with no need to take profits, but he does not think it will outperform over the next 12-18 months at this price, and a dip back toward $890 would be a buy again. He tracks every ranking change in a spreadsheet for transparency, showing the 21 September upgrade and the 13 October reiteration before this downgrade, which he dates to 9 November in the video. His call is COST HOLD, flipping from BUY. The video is short and single-stock: no other tickers are discussed.

calls.thesis: FLIP: BUY (21 Sep @ ~$890, reiterated 13 Oct) -> HOLD — stock ran to $1,060+, forward P/E over 42 vs his ~$833 DCF fair value (21% above FV); great Hall of Fame business to hold, but the rare cheap entry is gone and unlikely to outperform over the next 12-18 months.
calls.base_case: Performs in line with the market; no need to take profits.
calls.bull_case: Hall of Fame compounder; a dip back toward $890 would be a buy again.
calls.bear_case: Valuation stays elevated (P/E >42); no earnings catalyst drove the rally, just multiple expansion.
